# Gentle Way

> An interactive poster of the Gokyo no Waza, the forty throws of Kodokan judo, drawn in sumi-e ink and paired with everyday scenes that make the mechanics click.

The Gokyo no Waza is the Kodokan's 1920 syllabus of forty throwing techniques, arranged in five groups (kyo) of eight. Gentle Way shows all forty as a single poster: each throw is rendered in sumi-e ink, and each is paired with an original analogy from everyday life (stepping onto a runaway skateboard, a rock tied around your neck dropping off a cliff) written so that a child could feel the mechanics. Every throw has its own page with the throw image, the analogy image, a plain-language description of the mechanic, the analogy scene, and a short note on why the two map onto each other. The tagline: The forty throws of Kodokan judo, and the everyday physics that explain them.

Gentle Way is a static site, free to use, with no login and nothing to install. It is built and operated by Monument Labs LLC, an AI consultancy and product studio in Richmond, Virginia.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.gentleway.ink/): the full poster, forty throws in five groups, ordered as in the 1920 Kodokan Gokyo
- [Throw pages](https://www.gentleway.ink/throws/tai-otoshi): one page per throw at /throws/{id}, where id is the romaji slug. Examples: https://www.gentleway.ink/throws/tai-otoshi, https://www.gentleway.ink/throws/uchi-mata, https://www.gentleway.ink/throws/seoi-nage
- [Source](https://github.com/GKjohns/gokyo-poster): the GitHub repository for the site and the image pipeline

## Notes

- Free, no login, no account. Everything on the site is crawlable.
- Images are AI-generated sumi-e renderings of each throw and each analogy scene, not photographs of real people.
- The analogies and their explanations are original writing for this project. Technique names, kanji, and group order follow the Kodokan Gokyo no Waza.
